question: Within the fixed 17-record inventory, did any record directly demonstrate that androgen exposure or androgen-state manipulation decreases intestinal ABCG2?
decision_rule: Direct suppression is demonstrated only by a record classified as an in_vivo or in_vitro direct test with target_outcome=decrease. Absence of such a row yields NOT_DEMONSTRATED_IN_FIXED_INVENTORY, not a universal literature-absence conclusion.
forbidden_inferences: No direct androgen-suppression study exists outside this fixed inventory.
Testosterone physiologically increases intestinal ABCG2 in humans.
Healthy-human intestinal ABCG2 has no sex difference.
Estradiol establishes a female intestinal ABCG2 baseline advantage.
Male or androgen-dominant physiology imposes a quantified gut-lumen export ceiling.
The broader androgen–urate prior is unsupported.
The inventory establishes a clomiphene mechanism or treatment implication.

records.citation: Hoque KM, Halperin Kuhns VL, et al. (2020), Nature Communications, DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-16525-w, PMID 32488095
records.retained_finding: Q140K+/+ mice had 78% lower jejunal ABCG2 by Western blot than WT, compared with a 44% renal reduction.
records.boundary: Genotype-stressed mouse evidence; androgen exposure was not manipulated and the result is not a healthy-human baseline.

records.citation: Sakamoto K et al. (2018), PLOS ONE, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0209049, PMID 30557349
records.boundary: Androgen-deprivation and serum-urate context; intestinal ABCG2 was not measured in the inventory extraction.

records.citation: Liu L, Zhao T, Shan L, Cao L, Zhu X, Xue Y (2021), Nutrition & Metabolism, DOI 10.1186/s12986-021-00583-y, PMID 34144706
records.retained_finding: Nominal 100 µM estradiol benzoate increased Caco-2 ABCG2 mRNA at 48 hours without a dose-dependent response; 50 µM LY294002 partially blocked the response.
records.boundary: Pharmacological Caco-2 estradiol result; not an androgen test or a physiological intestinal effect size.

records.citation: Slepnev AA, Abalenikhina YV, Popova NM, Shchulkin AV, Yakusheva EN (2023), Biochemistry (Moscow) Supplement Series A, DOI 10.1134/S1990747823050100
records.retained_finding: Nominal 1, 10, and 100 µM testosterone increased Caco-2 ABCG2 after 24 hours; PXR/FXR inhibitor conditions reduced the increase, which remained above control.
records.boundary: Official-abstract-tier Caco-2 result; it does not establish physiological exposure or exclude androgen-receptor involvement.

records.citation: Tanaka Y, Slitt AL, Leazer TM, Maher JM, Klaassen CD (2005), Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications, DOI 10.1016/j.bbrc.2004.10.182, PMID 15567169
records.boundary: The old extraction did not isolate an intestinal ABCG2 outcome under androgen manipulation.

records.citation: Naud J et al. (2008), Drug Metabolism and Disposition, DOI 10.1124/dmd.107.017996, PMID 17855625
records.boundary: Sex-stratified nephrectomy disease model; no direct androgen × intestinal ABCG2 test was retained.

records.citation: Jeong H et al. (2015), Biochimica et Biophysica Acta, DOI 10.1016/j.bbagrm.2015.01.006, PMID 25615818
records.boundary: Androgen-withdrawal mechanism in prostate cancer cells, not intestinal epithelium.

records.citation: Yahyaoui R, T'Sjoen G, et al. (2008), Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism, DOI 10.1210/jc.2007-2467, PMID 18349066
records.boundary: Hormone-therapy urate/FEUA context; intestinal ABCG2 was not measured.

records.citation: Halperin Kuhns VL, Woodward OM (2020), International Journal of Molecular Sciences, DOI 10.3390/ijms21124269, PMID 32560040
records.boundary: Review-level framing; not a direct experiment.

records.citation: MacLean C, Moenning U, Reichel A, Fricker G (2008), Drug Metabolism and Disposition, DOI 10.1124/dmd.108.020859, PMID 18378562
records.retained_finding: The rat intestinal transporter-expression scan reported no sex-specific difference.
records.boundary: Healthy-rat qualitative null; no androgen manipulation and no healthy-human effect-size estimate.

records.citation: Drozdzik M et al. (2014), Molecular Pharmaceutics, DOI 10.1021/mp500330y, PMID 25158075
records.boundary: Human intestinal abundance study without androgen manipulation in the retained extraction; not a direct target test.

records.citation: Hosoyamada M, Takiue Y, et al. (2010), Nucleosides, Nucleotides & Nucleic Acids, DOI 10.1080/15257770.2010.494651, PMID 20589576
records.boundary: Mouse renal urate-transporter experiment; intestinal ABCG2 was not measured.

records.citation: Takiue Y et al. (2011), Nucleosides, Nucleotides & Nucleic Acids, DOI 10.1080/15257770.2011.551172, PMID 21360409
records.boundary: Mouse kidney and female-hormone context; not an androgen × intestinal ABCG2 test.

records.citation: Hak AE, Choi HK (2008), Arthritis Research & Therapy, DOI 10.1186/ar2519, PMID 18822120
records.boundary: Menopause/hormone-use serum-urate context; intestinal ABCG2 was not measured.

records.citation: Unresolved legacy row labelled KNIGHT/ENIGI prospective cohorts
records.boundary: The original row lacked a stable author, title, DOI, or PMID identity and contributes no evidence.

records.citation: Establishment of sex difference in circulating uric acid is associated with higher testosterone and lower SHBG in adolescent boys (2021), Scientific Reports, DOI 10.1038/s41598-021-96959-4, PMCID PMC8405811
records.boundary: Longitudinal serum-urate association; no intervention and no intestinal ABCG2 measurement.

records.citation: Halperin Kuhns VL et al. (2020), FASEB Journal abstract, DOI 10.1096/fasebj.2020.34.s1.06423
records.boundary: Renal-transporter conference abstract; not an intestinal androgen experiment.
